set.typical_award_size: Initial capitalization of $300,000 from the City general fund, required by the March 26, 2026 stipulated judgment (People of the State of California and HCD v. City of Hollister) and carried into the adopted 2023-2031 Housing Element as Policy Action H5.12. The fund must support housing for extremely low, very low and low income households, including migrant housing, emergency shelters, supportive housing, single-room occupancy and transitional housing. Award form (grant or loan), per-project limits and the application procedure are to be set in a program document approved by HCD. Any money remaining five years after deposit transfers to the State Building Homes and Jobs Trust Fund unless HCD agrees otherwise. On June 22, 2026 the City Council adopted a resolution approving the Housing Trust Guidelines and a FY 2026-27 budget adjustment moving $300,000 from General Fund 101 to the HOME Program Revolving Loan Fund 809 (5-0 roll call), and directed staff to submit the guidelines to HCD for review. The guideline text is attached to the agenda item but could not be opened (eScribe attachments behind a bot check), so award form and limits remain unconfirmed.
set.next_deadline: No open round as of November 10, 2026. Guidelines and the $300,000 deposit were approved June 22, 2026 and sent to HCD for review; no HCD approval or funding round has been posted. Contact housing@hollister.ca.gov for status.
set.cycle_notes: Housing Trust Guidelines and $300,000 budget adjustment approved by City Council June 22, 2026 (special meeting item 6.2, moved by Resendiz, seconded by Picha, 5-0); guidelines pending HCD review under the March 26, 2026 stipulated judgment.
set.layering_notes: This will be the only city-controlled capital source for affordable development in Hollister; there is no inclusionary in-lieu fund (Chapter 17.36 requires on-site units) and the former redevelopment agency's housing assets are limited to a Housing Division loan and resale monitoring portfolio (Successor Agency page opened). At $300,000 it is predevelopment-scale money; realistic use is a predevelopment loan or local match that strengthens a TCAC, HCD or AHSC application, layered under county sources (San Benito County PLHA, HHAP, CMFA conduit bonds) and Housing Authority of the County of Santa Cruz PBVs. The five-year sunset creates pressure to commit funds quickly, which favors shovel-ready sponsors. H5.12 also commits the City to annual developer meetings, one-on-one technical assistance and support letters. The $300,000 sits in the HOME Program Revolving Loan Fund 809 alongside HOME program income, so trust awards may carry HOME-style terms; confirm once HCD approves the guidelines. Sources opened: judgment text (oag.ca.gov Exhibit B), adopted Housing Element PDF, and the June 22, 2026 City Council minutes on eScribe.
set.audit_note: Follow-up Nov 10, 2026: June 22, 2026 Council minutes (eScribe PostMinutes view) confirm adoption of the Housing Trust Guidelines and the $300,000 transfer to HOME Revolving Loan Fund 809, with the guidelines sent to HCD. Guideline PDF (eScribe DocumentId 22444) not readable. funding_type kept as other until the guidelines state grant or loan.

set.typical_award_size: Municipal Code Chapter 4.240, Development Impact Fee Deferral Program, was created by ordinance in October 2024 (Council supported it unanimously at first reading; second reading October 22, 2024) so affordable projects no longer need Council approval for each impact fee deferral or waiver request. Per search excerpts of the ordinance text and staff reports (city site blocked, not opened): eligible projects are new residential developments with at least 50 percent of units affordable to lower income households; deferrable fees include the Park and Recreation Facilities Tax, Traffic Mitigation Fee, Service Area Park Mitigation Fee, Quimby Fee, CIDS Park Fee, General Capital Improvements Tax and Fire Facility and Equipment Fee; deferred fees plus accrued interest are secured by a recorded deed of trust, with a deferral term of up to 55 years described in the Planning Commission packet. Separately, 100 percent affordable projects are exempt from the $13,000 development agreement fee, and Riverside Apartments and Westview Village received Council-granted partial fee waivers.
set.affordability_requirement: Chapter 4.240 deferral: at least 50 percent of units restricted to lower income households (search excerpts of the ordinance, not opened). Partial fee waivers: all-affordable projects.

100% affordable developments (partial waiver, development agreement fee exemption)

set.cycle_notes: Chapter 4.240 adopted October 2024 (second reading October 22, 2024). Used for Arrive Ventura (297 units, 104 affordable; Council action May 13, 2025, Quimby fee excluded) and requested for College Community Courts (February 25, 2025 Quimby fee deferral).
set.layering_notes: Fee deferral, not forgiveness: fees plus interest come due later, secured by a deed of trust, so lenders and TCAC underwriting must carry the deferred obligation. Council items for Arrive Ventura (May 2025) and College Community Courts (February 2025) show larger requests, and the Quimby fee, still went to Council after adoption. Ventura Housing Authority CEO Jeff Lambert said the program lets sponsors plan ahead (Ojai Valley News, October 2024). Fee relief is local public funds for prevailing wage purposes. Needs confirmation because cityofventura.ca.gov returns 403; the 2021-2029 Housing Element (HCD site) and the Ojai Valley News report were opened, and ordinance details come from search excerpts of city PDFs (DocumentCenter 41962 ordinance language, 41976 Planning Commission packet, 42235 October 22, 2024 agenda item, 44572 May 13, 2025 agenda item).
